Though this matter is listed for admission, with consent of both parties, the same is taken up for hearing.
2. This appeal is filed against the judgment and award dated 05.03.2022 passed by the Additional MACT and Additional Senior Civil Judge, Bidar, in MVC No.14 of 2021.
3. The injured claimant filed a claim application claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest.
The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, granted the compensation of Rs.6,28,447/- with interest at the rate of 9 percent per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6620 HC-KAR 4.
Aggrieved by the said order, this appeal is preferred by the appellant-claimant in which it is mainly contended that the petitioner-claimant sustained crush injury to his right hand.
As such, his right wrist was amputated.
The doctor assessed the disability as 60% to the whole body, but, the Tribunal has taken only 20% disability.
The claimant was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has taken his income as Rs.11,000/- per month.

He was admitted as an inpatient for 7 Swamidas S/O Babu vs Malla Reddy S/O Siddareddy And Anr on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56228486/

sentences.text: Meager amounts were granted under the other heads.
Therefore, requested for enhancement in compensation.

5. Heard the arguments of both sides.
6.
The petitioner-claimant has stated that he was aged 34 years at the time of accident, doing agricultural work and labour work, and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
However, he has not filed any documents to prove his income.
The petitioner-claimant met with an accident on 26.11.2019.

As per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Rs.13,250/- is to be taken as his notional income and as he NC: 2025:KHC-K:6620 HC-KAR was aged 33 years as per Exhibit P7-discharge summary, the multiplier is to be taken as 16.
Admittedly, the petitioner- claimant suffered crush injury to his right wrist and it resulted in loss of vascularity and loss of sensation.
He was hospitalized for 7 days.
As it is the case of amputation, the doctor assessed the disability as 60%.

7. The learned counsel for the appellant-claimant has contended that the petitioner-claimant was working as an agricultural labour and he cannot discharge his duties due to amputation and therefore, it is to be taken as functional disability.
Learned counsel for respondent submitted that the Tribunal has taken 20% towards functional disability and therefore, it needs no interference.
Admittedly, as it is a case of amputation to right wrist, this Court finds it reasonable to take the disability assessed by the doctor i.e. 60% to the whole body.

The claimant is also entitled for 40%
towards future prospects.
So, the loss of future income comes to Rs.21,36,960/- (13,250 + 40% x 12 x 16 x 60%).
The Tribunal has already granted Rs.76,047/- towards medical expenses and it needs no interference.

This Court finds it NC: 2025:KHC-K:6620 HC-KAR reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.50,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.40,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
The petitioner-claimant might not have attended any other work at least for a period of four months due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
Therefore, he is entitled for income of Rs.53,000/- (13,250 x 4) for the loss of income during laid up period.

Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled for the compensation of Rs.24,56,007/-
with interest at 6% per annum as against Rs.6,28,447/- awarded by the Tribunal.
8.

The award of compensation passed by the Tribunal is modified as under:
 Heads Amount in Rs.
 1. Loss of future income 21,36,960/-
 2. Medical expense 76,047/-
 3. Pain and Suffering 1,00,000/-
 4. Loss of amenities 50,000/-
 5. Attendant charges, extra 40,000/-
 nourishment and diet food  6. Loss of earning during the laid up 53,000/-
 period

Total 24,56,007/-

In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The appellant-claimant is entitled for the total compensation of Rs.24,56,007/- with interest at 6 percent per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

(iii) The respondent-insurance company has already deposited the awarded amount before the Tribunal, and therefore, they are directed to deposit the enhanced amount of Rs.18,27,560/- with interest at 6% per annum within one month from the date of copy of this order.
(iv) On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with the interest accrued on it.
